evidence: TH jurisdiction seed > Skill Development Fund: the contribution over the year’s month-end headcounts and the trained count. Formula read 2026-10-07 on dsd.go.th (Department of Skill Development guidance for employers in the compulsory scheme): the lowest statutory minimum daily wage × 30 × the employees short of training 50% of the year's average headcount × the months with 100 or more employees ÷ 100, paid with Sor Tor 2 within March of the next year. Round 10 (obligation rules.amount over company facts and headcount_months): raised with the December run over the year's twelve month-end headcounts; the trained count is the entity fact sdf_trained_employees; the wage base is 337 baht, the lowest provincial rate of the version's minimum_wage table (the guidance's 'lowest uniform minimum wage', set when the country had one rate). The Sor Tor 2 return stays SKILL_DEVELOPMENT_CONTRIBUTION; the initial direct-gazette retrieval of the 1% rate announcement failed (superseded by the primary-copy verification below). Primary notice recovered 2026-10-10: DSD official inspection manual กสพ.-01-2568, https://sdfund.dsd.go.th/Uploads/mas_document/127/file/คู่มือปฏิบัติงานการตรวจแบบแสดงการส่งเงินสมทบกองทุนฯ%20(สท_compressed%20(1)_95ad28d6-0c5a-4a31-aad5-9531d4fd44c4.pdf?uu_id=2M847, appendix PDF pages 29-30 reproduces the Ministry notice signed 1 July 2015, gazetted 23 July 2015 (vol.132 special part172 Ngor, pp.11-12). Visually read clauses 5-8: 1% contribution, monthly base equal to lowest statutory daily minimum times 30, untrained shortfall times the applicable months, annual payment with return within March. PDF page31 reproduces 30 December 2020 amendment to clause9 requiring electronic filing with paper fallback for unavailable or failed electronic service. This closes the previously unread rate-notice gap. Applicability remains to audit: the separate 9 April 2015 scope notice on PDF page28 excludes specified agricultural activities without all-year employment or related activities, private schools, private higher education and non-profit foundations/charities; these categories cannot be inferred from headcount alone. Formula correction 2026-10-10: all seven versions now average month-end headcounts from the first month reaching 100 through December, include subsequent below-threshold months, use that whole window for the month multiplier, and discard fractional training targets. Previous whole-year averaging, upward target rounding and counting only months individually above 100 were incorrect. Official manual printed pp.18-19 / PDF pp.21-22 and scope-notice clause5 confirm the window. Regression uses the published second example (June-December sum 783, seven months, training target 55), plus pre-threshold exclusions, sufficient training, a one-person shortfall and no qualifying month. Source evidence is recovered; employer-category exclusions remain a distinct coverage gap. Scope integration 2026-10-10: all seven entity schemas declare sdf_exemption with NONE, SEASONAL_AGRICULTURE, PRIVATE_SCHOOL, PRIVATE_HIGHER_EDUCATION, NON_PROFIT and STATE_BODY. The category requires evidence of the exact legal conditions; seasonal agriculture excludes year-round employment or related activities, and non-profit status requires no economic-profit objective. Exempt categories suppress fund payment, registration, annual return and course-certification duties; NONE or an undeclared category retains ordinary liability. Existing late-payment obligations are not suppressed by a later category change. Regression exercises each category and each affected duty in every version, plus the ordinary employer contribution. Customer-specific exemption evidence is not inferred or fabricated.
